scope: Provenance, source-space coordinate consistency, original mesh topology, hemisphere labels and limited nerve/bone collision sampling. NativePacking covers the v2 base; v3ContextPacking records additions. Not independent expert anatomical validation.

sideAssignment.method: Connected components of original triangle-index graph; each component assigned only if its complete vertex bounding box is outside the septum reference plane +/-2 mm band.
sideAssignment.sideMeaning: Positive R relative to reference plane is patient right; negative R is patient left.
sideAssignment.interpretation: Reliable coarse side assignment for these spatially separated components. It does not identify a precise midsagittal plane, establish anatomical boundaries, or improve source segmentation accuracy.

nativePacking.note: Geometry checks are not expert anatomical validation.

sourceSelection.priorityDecision: Use P41-16 donor labels in their native coordinate scene for source-based nuclei, BodyParts3D for the missing bilateral insula/internal capsule in a separately sourced scene, and UW CT for skull-base foramina in its own scene. Do not merge these disparate spaces without validated registration.
sourceSelection.anatomicalAccuracyClaim: Source provenance and numerical coordinate consistency are verified. This is not independent expert anatomical validation, and does not establish complete or error-free nuclear boundaries.

sources.name: NextBrain donor P41-16 (case 2), registered histology label blocks
sources.status: asset produced; nucleus labels only with native background
sources.licenseEvidence: Official Figshare API lists CC0 and directly links the UCL registered-data repositories including P41-16. The MIT license of the separate web viewer is not used as evidence for data permission.
sources.format: 40 uint16 NIfTI label blocks with individual native affines; corresponding donor T2w MRI and block-index volume
sources.originalSampling: Histology reconstruction uses 0.1 mm in-plane grids, 0.25 or 0.5 mm section spacing before registration scaling. Ex vivo MRI approximately 0.4 mm isotropic. NIfTI header spacings after transforms vary by block.
sources.headerUnitsNote: P41 NIfTI xyzt_units is unspecified; units are interpreted in millimetres from the published MRI protocol and documented RAS transforms, not inferred from voxel indices alone.
sources.geometry: 33 label segments (29 nuclear targets, 4 source residual/white-matter context labels); raw float32 positions and uint32 triangle indices, RAS mm. Target labels marching cubes level0.5 at every source voxel. No smoothing, filling, mirroring, fitting or component deletion.
sources.geometryContext: Context labels are sampled every fourth source voxel in each axis; exact displaySpacingMm is stored per part. This is not uniformly 0.4 mm because the source section direction has larger spacing.
limits: Single donor hemisphere. No bilateral reconstruction is claimed.
No original label for internal-capsule IDs73,115,204,258 in these blocks.
Blocks can leave seams or overlap; no seam welding or invented interpolation performed. Source boundary open mesh edges are retained.
Tiny local labels447,464,520 must not be described as complete nuclei. All segment completeNucleusClaim flags are false.
Source context labels580 and662 are residual tissue labels within a partition; they do not contain the other labelled nuclei and do not form complete pons/medulla envelopes.
Published landmark registration error about0.99±0.51mm across250 pairs is a dataset-level result, not a per-label accuracy guarantee.
No complete cranial nerve pathways emerge from these nucleus-only assets.
sources.coordinateValidationMeaning: 239 non-placeholder author ontology locations were transformed into native block coordinates:213 exactly hit the corresponding label voxel and all239 were within1mm of it. All40 block affines agree with official display transforms after only display-plane rotations and source slice-order reversals, max slice-coordinate error3.51e-6 voxels. These tests validate coordinates, not anatomical boundary accuracy.

sources.name: NextBrain 3dAtlas maximum-probability volume
sources.status: research evidence only; not proposed as complete nuclei
sources.content: 333 non-background labels; one pooled left-oriented hemisphere. Authors flip3right hemispheres and combine with2left hemispheres; retained cortex name ctx-rh-insula is an ontology identifier, not the volume orientation.
limitations: Argmax gives the most probable label in each voxel, not a full probability-envelope boundary. Small competing nuclear labels shrink strongly.
The large LUT includes labels absent from the actual image.
No added mirror should be presented as a real second hemisphere.

limitations: Symmetric population template, not an individual bilateral brain; cannot model actual lateral asymmetry.
No fine brainstem nuclei and no independent internal-capsule partition.
Do not transfer coordinates to MNI6 or Z-Anatomy by identity or an unvalidated affine.

foraminaAndInsulaResearch.purpose: Source-only additions for educational offline NeuroAtlas; no guessed foraminal rings or fitted anatomy
conclusions: Original existing skeletal.glb contains whole source bone meshes, no independently labeled bony foramen rim objects.

UW provides author-segmented bilateral foramen ovale/rotundum/spinosum and vidian canal volume labels with bone from a 6-subject synthetic CT template. These are volume-label boundaries, not separately traced bony rims.
DBCLS official 4.3 download provides source-labeled bilateral entire insula and internal capsule, with same-source basal/deep nuclei and selected cortical neighbors.
The two additions must be independent source coordinate spaces unless an explicit, validated registration is available. No registration/deformation was applied here.
No dataset located in this bounded research establishes a completely error-free, complete skull-base rim and all-nerve/course atlas.

candidates.title: Automated atlas-based segmentation for skull base surgical planning
candidates.sourceType: 6-subject synthetic CT template; manual reference segmentation agreed on by otolaryngologist and neuroradiologist per paper
candidates.nativeSpace: Segmentation RAS / CT LPS; convert CT physical coordinates by diag(-1,-1,1) only

geometryMethod.faceWinding: gradient_direction=ascent; positive signed volume / outward winding
geometryMethod.padding: one zero voxel to close outer array boundary
geometryMethod.coordinates: Original source RAS mm; no deformation or registration

validation: Eight source-CT overlay figures for left and right foramen ovale, spinosum, rotundum and vidian canal. No registration fitted.
Every labeled voxel samples within CT physical extent; finite CT intensity fractions equal 1.0 for all 14 segments.
Foramina ovale, rotundum and spinosum each have two nonempty connected components consistent with left and right; vidian canal has two large components plus a one-voxel island.
All original small islands are retained. No segmentation cleanup or anatomical repair was applied.
limits: Small foramina have few source voxels and 1.25 mm through-plane label resolution. Polygon precision does not improve that resolution.
The paper reports less favorable transferred segmentation usability for foramen rotundum/spinosum; this is not an error-free atlas.
No independently labeled true osseous rim, no explicit completeness guarantee for full canal length.

Bone label is cropped anterior skull-base/fossa anatomy, not a whole skull. Marching-cubes closes label regions at array crop boundaries, which are computational cut faces and must not be labeled natural bone surface.
It does not include jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal, internal acoustic meatus, stylomastoid foramen, foramen magnum or superior orbital fissure as separate labels.
No mandibular/maxillary nerves labeled, so this source cannot independently prove V3/V2 passage.
